message:
docs(history): a rejected tool call is not a result either

I said the 0.2.118 installer could not be restored. It was already there -- copied at
17:10:45, byte-identical to the staged payload. The copy had run and something after
it was refused; I reported from the refusal without looking at the file.

I also read that refusal as the user's decision. It was the harness classifier. Those
are different events and only one of them means stop.

Fourth instance today of the same mistake: a missing result: line read as success,
suites that print no PASS lines vanishing into a total, a PASS count that was a
stopping point, and now this. The rule gets one more line -- a command that changes a
file is checked by looking at the file.

Also narrows the C1 wording to what the logs actually prove: the stop request failed.
Parent/child state mapping is a hypothesis, and attempts with no log entry are not
counted as failures.
